concepts.definition: An operation-evidence plan binding one owner-selected Product Definition, the complete companion population of one exact upstream release-matched cohort, and owner-selected consumer bindings. Product Definition retains composition ownership; the cohort and Product release records retain release/member identity. Invocation, plan and result are not persistent dependency declarations, registries or locks.

grounding.quote:
An invocation selection and its derived plan and result
are operation evidence, not another persistent dependency declaration,
registry or lock.

concepts.label: Complete Consumer Update Plan and operation

concepts.definition: Manager outcomes are predicate-specific refinements of the referenced core result algebra, adding no core value. Effects concern whether an intended external effect occurred; admission concerns lawful admission and activation on the exact subject and basis; construction availability concerns whether a candidate is available. Effect value and whether the effect's end is established are distinct coordinates.

grounding.quote:
each
for its own predicate; the cause of an outcome selects its value, and the
mapping adds no core value

concepts.label: Manager operation result domains

concepts.definition: PRODUCT_DEFINITION declares ownership of urn:stdo:bounded-context:semantic-resolution under the selected complete STDO basis. A term is an occurrence's lexical label, not a context-free concept identity. A bounded context is an explicitly identified semantic scope whose governed vocabulary, concepts and relations are jointly interpretable under named authority. A concept reference exactly resolves an authority-owned meaning under a selected basis without creating meaning or authority.

grounding.quote:
A concept reference is an exact,
resolvable reference to a meaning owned by an authority under a selected
basis; the reference locates that meaning and mints neither the meaning nor
its authority (P1, P3, P6).

concepts.label: Bounded-context semantic resolution

concepts.definition: Every material term occurrence has semantic address (term, bounded-context identity, owning authority, selected basis, governed scope). Resolution identifies scope and the nearest explicit context declaration, then exact basis and applicable authorities, then admitted local definitions and explicit imports, then every applicable owner-authorised override or disambiguation; admission requires exactly one remaining concept.

grounding.quote:
4. apply every applicable owner-authorised override or disambiguation; and
5. admit the occurrence only when exactly one concept remains.
(term, bounded-context identity, owning authority, selected basis, governed scope)

concepts.label: Semantic address and ordered resolution

concepts.definition: Four explicit owner-authorised cross-context relation kinds are distinguished. Semantic Import adopts unchanged meaning for a declared target scope under FOUNDATIONS' import rule. Semantic Translation declares directional meaning change and loss and is not an import. Semantic Equivalence requires governing authorities to establish equality while concepts retain their owners and contexts; opposing translations or equal spelling do not prove it. Semantic Disambiguation selects one meaning for one scope without equating competitors; an externally owned selected meaning requires its declared import, translation or equivalence. Specialisation is a directional translation preserving declared source meaning while narrowing admissible instances or adding target constraints.

grounding.quote: | Semantic Disambiguation | not an import: it selects one meaning for one scope and does not make competing concepts equal. Where the selected concept is owned in another bounded context, it enters that scope only by the import, translation or equivalence its carrier declares (§6) |

A specialisation is a directional translation whose target preserves the
declared source meaning while narrowing its admissible instances or adding
target-context constraints.

concepts.label: Semantic cross-context relation kinds

concepts.definition: A local axiom, override or disambiguation is bound through a decision-carrying URI, its existing lawful authority, applicable overridden clause or ambiguity, and exact scope. Overlay metadata locates and exposes a source-owned decision for checking; it does not create that decision or restate its meanings.

grounding.quote:
The overlay metadata makes the relation
discoverable and checkable; it neither restates the source-owned meanings
nor mints the decision (P6).

concepts.label: Local constitutional binding

concepts.definition: A Product-owned accepted declaration of the shared frame set through which finite actors collectively engage one governed Product scope or outcome. It binds exact reference-frame law and optional profile basis; admitting authorities and scopes; frame declarations and evaluation inventory; actor rules and capability envelopes; semantic, evaluation, operation and decision grants; result, conjunction, translation and coverage relations; lifecycle activation triggers and invalidation law. The referenced declaration owns this content; reference_frame_bases entries merely locate it and its authority relation.

grounding.quote:
A Project Reference-Frame Basis is the Product-owned accepted declaration
of the shared frame set through which finite actors collectively engage one
governed Product scope or outcome (P0, P6; rc.2
#collective-reference-frame-basis).

concepts.label: Project Reference-Frame Basis

concepts.definition: An execution-scoped binding of one agent to an applicable frame declaration or active configuration, exact evaluation, subject, basis, evidence boundary and capability envelope. A ticket or other authorised instruction carries the activation packet; Product Definition retains the durable shared basis. Activation does not mutate the overlay, register agents, assign permanent frames or persist temporary active configurations.

grounding.quote:
An Agent Frame
Activation is the execution-scoped binding of one agent to an applicable
frame declaration or active configuration, an exact evaluation, subject,
basis, evidence boundary and capability envelope;

concepts.label: Agent Frame Activation

concepts.definition: PRODUCT_DEFINITION owns urn:stdo:bounded-context:build-tenancy under the selected complete STDO basis. Build tenancy is one constitutional WHAT realised by one or more independent project-owned HOW tenants; one tenant is the singleton case, and more than one independent realisation of the same WHAT is multi-build-tenancy. SPEC_METHOD §11 owns the build tenant, this relation and tenant binding through an explicit owner relation; TICKETS §4 owns the multi-build-tenant work-item relation.

grounding.quote:
In this context build tenancy is that one-or-more relation; one tenant is
its singleton case, and multi-build-tenancy begins when the same WHAT has
more than one independent realisation (P3, P2; rc.2
#what-how-and-work-carriers).

concepts.label: Build tenancy

concepts.definition: what.intent and what.product each locate one canonical entrypoint of the current constitutional WHAT; what.specification may locate multiple requirement/specification surfaces. how.build_tenants is the canonical Tenant Registry, with stable tenant identities and root, design and implementation locators. how.common binds a Common Build-Tenant Surface: realisation law explicitly adopted across more than one tenant.

grounding.quote:
The Tenant Registry is the canonical `how.build_tenants` collection for the
product's independent HOW realisations.

concepts.label: Constitutional WHAT and tenant HOW locators

concepts.definition: ticketing.goals locates current work-wave orientation; ticketing.tickets locates the durable ticket root and at least backlog, active and completed lanes; ticketing.comments locates commentary; optional ticketing.sprints locates bounded execution-batch manifests. Goals own the bounded wave, ticket state remains ticket authority, and comments are non-authoritative. This section binds locations; SPEC_METHOD §4 and TICKETS determine carrier selection.

grounding.quote:
Goals own the bounded work wave, ticket state stays ticket
authority, and comments stay non-authoritative commentary (P6, P3). Which
carrier a given work item takes is SPEC_METHOD §4 and the [TICKETS](TICKETS.md) member;
this section binds where each carrier kind lives.

concepts.label: Work-carrier location bindings

concepts.definition: Recursive discovery finds stdo_*.json at workspace root and arbitrarily deep nested project roots within the selected workspace boundary. Explicit composition entries relate independently identified Product Definitions through current target locator, expected stable target_definition_id, directed relation authority and one or more exact governing contracts.

grounding.quote:
Directory nesting creates no implicit inheritance, ownership, composition
or constitutional override. Parent and child definitions stay independent
until `composition` explicitly relates them.

concepts.label: Product discovery and explicit composition

concepts.definition: Minimum exact-basis semantic-conformance cases distinguish Frame evaluation context from consumer runtime carrier, Owner evaluation family from semantic/decision owner, immutable Product from mutable Product Definition, and build Tenant from hosted/customer/account/runtime/data tenancy. User remains unresolved among Product role, human, principal, account, actor, operator and data subject until downstream authority defines or explicitly relates meanings. CONFORMANCE may index these cases without redefining them.

grounding.quote: | `User` | a Product role, human person, identity principal, account, actor, operator or data subject | unresolved until downstream authority defines or explicitly relates the applicable meanings |

concepts.label: Semantic-resolution conformance cases

concepts.definition: STDO-SURFACE-001 describes modular authorship with singular authority: one owning member per law, other members consuming it by reference, and operation only as one complete released method version. A released cut identifies exact member set/digests, review basis, human acceptance and immutable identity. Method-owned law concerns normative construction algebra, authority, abstract state/transitions, admissibility, necessary causal order and evidence invariants; consumers own concrete Product realisation.

grounding.quote:
STDO-SURFACE-001. The shared methodology is modular in authorship and
singular in authority. Each law has one owning member; other members
consume it by reference. The members become operative only as one complete
released version of the method

concepts.label: Complete released method constitution

concepts.definition: Compressions, templates, comments, candidate work, installed copies and mutable source are derived, evidential or authoring surfaces rather than selectable partial constitutions. Released/installed derived carriers include bootstraps, indexes and projected frames, with source and watched-index paths/digests identifying freshness dependencies.

grounding.quote:
Compressions, templates,
comments, candidate work, installed copies and mutable source are derived,
evidential or authoring surfaces. They cannot become a selectable partial
constitution and cannot reinterpret the owning members (P3, P6).

concepts.label: Derived method surfaces

concepts.definition: Every method-defined product starts from the exact-cut PRODUCT_DEFINITION_TEMPLATE.json copied to its definition root as stdo_default.json for a singleton default or stdo_<label>.json for a named definition. Default scaffold: exact constitution.stdo.basis in a shared versioned store; specification/GOALS.md, INTENT.md, PRODUCT.md and requirements/; build_tenants/common/ and default/; .ai-workspace/sprints/, tickets/{backlog,active,completed}/ and comments/. These are starter defaults selected or replaced by URI bindings.

grounding.quote:
Every product defined under this method begins from
`templates/PRODUCT_DEFINITION_TEMPLATE.json`, copied to the product's
definition root as `stdo_default.json` for a singleton default project or
as `stdo_<label>.json` for a named product definition.

concepts.label: Product bootstrap and default scaffold

concepts.definition: The member reports predecessor conservation by rc.2 SPEC_METHOD anchor: overlay/layout (§1), required relations (§2), constitutional sufficiency (§3), manager (§4), complete update (§4 subsection), semantic resolution (§5), local bindings (§6), collective basis (§7), WHAT/HOW (§8), discovery/composition (§9), conformance (§10), singular surface (§11), bootstrap (§12). Carrying renames IDENTITY_METHOD→IDENTITY, RELEASE_METHOD→RELEASE, GLOSSARY_GUIDE→GLOSSARY, REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD→REFERENCE_FRAME and STDO_REFERENCE_FRAME_BASELINE→Executive baseline; 'standard' becomes 'member'. Agent Frame Activation replaces an ambiguous 'execution binding'; the source authoring path is generalised. Routes and carried names are provenance rather than dispositions.

grounding.quote:
Every row
is restated in this member's own text; a route is provenance only. Where
the predecessor named one of its own members, the tenant member that
receives the same law is named instead; this is carrying, not a
disposition, and is recorded in the row.

concepts.label: PRODUCT_DEFINITION predecessor-disposition claims

concepts.definition: The core consists of tier-1 and tier-2 members. Profiles are domain or operational specialisations. Tier-3 PROFILES owns the core/profile boundary, declared-binding rule and profile import rule, and indexes graph execution, software design, UX, world model and engagement baseline.

Tier 3. Owns the boundary between the core and the profiles, the
declared-binding rule and the import rule that every profile applies
(§1), and indexes the profiles (§2 to §6). A profile is a domain or
operational specialisation of the method; the members of tiers 1 and 2
are the core.

concepts.label: Core and profile categories

concepts.definition: A profile's declared binding specialises a core mechanism with direction, preserved meaning, narrowed scope and invalidation. This use of binding is distinct from Product profile-adoption binding and UX carrier-to-typed-contract binding. The declared-binding rule follows the shape of ODD-owned graph-native F_P/F_H specialisations; that provenance does not transfer ownership.

grounding.quote:
In this member "binding" means
that declared binding of a core mechanism; a Product's adoption binding is
[PRODUCT_DEFINITION §7](PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#7-collective-reference-frame-basis)'s,
and a carrier binding to a typed contract is [UX §7](UX.md#7-carrier-binding)'s;
the three are not interchanged.

concepts.label: Declared profile binding

It binds the FOUNDATIONS P0 bounded step to one vector/edge traversal and graph-native F_P/F_D/F_H shorthands; F_P/F_H specialise SPEC_METHOD §5. Its graph functions refine ACTIVATION §4, with §11.8 cumulative environment law as the specialised contract carrying earlier outputs. ODD §10 owns runtime/product/service responsibility layers; the worker's internal solution strategy remains outside the framework. PROFILES indexes these bindings without owning them.

grounding.quote:
Where another member says that
this section keeps the ODD binding, the binding is the one ODD states and
this section indexes (P0, P1).

concepts.definition: The reference frame is atomic at engagement altitude: activated/evaluated as one bounded context, potentially containing several semantic atoms and owner relations without merging them. An activated frame combines declared evaluation family, exact workspace/topology basis, finite material relations/coordinates, invariants/authorities, admissible evidence/exclusions and capability envelope, yielding one closed core result. Frame-set selection uses governed workspace/outcome, practice/failures, actor capabilities and human judgment, then bounded evaluations, required conjunction/translation, coverage ledger/residual uncertainty and empirical revision. Selection, activation, evaluation, conjunction, translation, coverage and revision are separate functions; a frame need not first contain a universal relationship theory.

grounding.quote:
"Atomic" is said at engagement altitude only. It does not assert that every
relation inside the frame is one irreducible semantic atom; a frame may
carry several semantic atoms and several owner relations without merging
their meaning or authority (P1, P3).

concepts.label: Frame as atomic engagement unit

concepts.definition: Declared lossless imports into reference-frame-evaluation come from member contexts because FOUNDATIONS, ACTIVATION and EVALUATION declare no bounded-context identity. FOUNDATIONS §2 supplies frame objects (evaluation/family/workspace/manifold/coordinate/topology/envelope/frame/activated frame/frame set/configuration/lens/role/persona/abstraction/component), ontology (subject/outcome/basis/material relation/evidence/actor/claim/judgment/residual), authority kinds and actor identity, disjointness/evaluation independence/assurance independence, and tuple ⟨Q,B,M,C,I,A,E,X,R,J,K,D⟩; §4 supplies core results/standing/not-performed/refinements and conjunction/composition with declared decision rule. ACTIVATION §§1–2 supply step intake/admission/applicability/measured context/activation/evaluation, §3 results/disposition, §7 closed-result reuse. EVALUATION §7 supplies frame/method qualification. These are referenced identities, not locally reconstructed definitions.

grounding.quote:
FOUNDATIONS, ACTIVATION and
EVALUATION declare no bounded-context identity, so each row's source
context is its member (P1, P3).

concepts.label: Declared frame-context import catalogue

conditions: A complete consumer update is proposed or applied.

grounding.quote:
Mutation requires
explicit acceptance of this exact plan and re-derives it; possession of its
digest alone grants no operation authority.

constraints.statement: The caller selects every native route and derived context in the claimed scope; proximity and empty discovery cannot supply selection. An empty derived-context population records owner selection of none, not established absence of semantic context. cohort-update presents the whole plan without consumer effects. Acceptance binds physical destinations, binding preimages, exact cohort bytes, companion annotated tags/commits/subtrees/inventories, replacement locators, native routes and declared derived-source observations, using the same canonical JSON hash rule. Already-installed status changes neither authority nor digest. Mutation requires explicit exact-plan acceptance and re-derivation; digest possession grants no authority. adopt, sync and fleet retain narrower contracts.
constraints.uncertainty: The prior canonical hashing rule and narrower command contracts are referenced but not supplied.

conditions: Before relying on companions and before consumer application.

grounding.quote:
It stages absent immutable installs, verifies
existing installs without repairing them in place, and preflights every
consumer target.

constraints.statement: Verify cohort dependency closure and every exact companion's definition, release record and admitted members before reliance; stage absent immutable installs, verify existing installs without in-place repair, and preflight every consumer target. Changes are confined to selected basis/schema, existing composition locators/contracts and selected native/install links. Historical installs and unrelated content remain available and unchanged; create no consumer-local checker and change no Product meaning or local semantic map. For each selected derived context, missing/ambiguous/changed/unavailable program, map or source evidence holds the complete update before any consumer effect. Needed semantic re-entry belongs to the source owner; the manager cannot relabel an old map current. Source freshness proves integrity, not semantic conformance or an independent semantic verdict.

conditions: Immutable staging has occurred or application is attempted.

grounding.quote:
The operation requires an exclusive consumer
write scope during application. It claims no crash-atomic transaction
across independent filesystem paths: abrupt process or host loss, or
unavailable rollback storage, requires recovery from the presented
preimages before the complete relation can be claimed (P5, P4b).

constraints.statement: After staging, recheck consumer preimages and source evidence. Report completion only after verifying every selected resulting binding and companion. Refusal before consumer effects retains prior state. Caught application failure restores affected preimages and cannot report completion; newly staged immutable installs may remain unused. Application requires exclusive consumer write scope. No crash-atomic cross-path transaction is claimed; abrupt process/host loss or unavailable rollback storage requires recovery from presented preimages before claiming the complete relation.

conditions: An operation has an intended external effect, including install, sync, mutating adopt, fleet adoption or complete consumer update.

grounding.quote:
Abrupt process or
  host loss, where no caught failure establishes that the update fell
  short, is `completion_unknown` (`indeterminate`), never `completed` or
  `not_effected`.

constraints.statement: For 'the intended effect occurred', completed maps to satisfied only with evidence establishing the full effect. Refusal before any effect is not_effected/falsified, with retained prior state as evidence and effect ended. Caught application failure is also not_effected/falsified because the update fell short and no later part is applied: verified restoration establishes the end; unverified restoration or unavailable rollback storage leaves the end unestablished, recorded as a residual naming needed verification, without changing the falsified value. Unused staged immutable installs are recorded as the part that occurred. Abrupt loss without a caught failure establishing shortfall is completion_unknown/indeterminate, neither completed nor not_effected. completion_unknown and not_effected with unestablished end require preimage recovery/reconciliation before repetition or claiming the complete relation.

conditions: A refusal is encountered.

grounding.quote:
It is `admission_refused(basis)` before the operation begins and
  `re_entry_requested(basis)` after, `invalid_basis` in both, and names
  the basis coordinate that fails and, for derived-context evidence, the
  source owner whose re-entry repairs it.

constraints.statement: A refusal also answers permission to apply the effect on the exact bound subject/basis. Before beginning it belongs to admission/activation; after beginning, including post-staging recheck, to construction availability. Missing explicit exact-plan acceptance or whole-selection fleet-write authorisation is missing operation authority: admission_refused(authority)/out_of_frame, naming required acceptance/authorisation and owner. Every other refusal has a basis cause, including Definition/preimage drift, stale plan, prior fail-closed conditions, ambiguous discovery lacking exact subject, escaping/broken path/locator/marker boundaries, and deficient derived evidence. Basis refusals map to admission_refused(basis) before beginning and re_entry_requested(basis) after, both invalid_basis, naming failing coordinate and, for derived evidence, source re-entry owner. Result consumers must not collapse refusal/failure into completion, completion_unknown into success/failure, known caught failure into undecided because restoration is unverified, or missing authority into defective basis.
constraints.uncertainty: The referenced earlier fail-closed list is unavailable; no additional members of that list are invented.

conditions: A command has no intended external effect, such as verify or adopt --dry-run.

grounding.quote:
A command without an intended
  external effect, such as `verify` or `adopt --dry-run`, has no value
  under Effects, and its refusal maps by cause as above.

constraints.statement: No Effects value applies. Refusals still map by cause. A reported subject counterexample, such as a missing, extra or changed member found by verify, falsifies that command's own predicate and is not a refusal.

grounding.quote:
A bounded context exists only when an owning authority declares its stable
identity, owner, selected basis and governed semantic scope.

constraints.statement: A context requires owner declaration of stable identity, owner, selected basis and governed semantic scope; a consuming member defines a concept there only by explicit owner relation. Filename, heading, index/glossary/schema value or bare URI does not constitute it. Equal spelling, capitalisation, shape, location, nesting, actor or implementation proves neither meaning/identity/equivalence/inheritance nor authority; different spelling proves no semantic difference. Such relations require semantic address or explicit authorised relation. Repositories, prompts, actors and nearby definitions do not accidentally declare contexts.

conditions: Resolution leaves zero or multiple applicable concepts at a material boundary.

grounding.quote:
Zero applicable concepts is unresolved meaning; more than one is ambiguous
meaning. Both fail closed at a material boundary:

constraints.statement: Zero means unresolved; multiple means ambiguous. Agents, designs, schemas, implementations, tests, translations and reviewers must not guess by familiarity/frequency/recency/nominal match or context-free glossary fallback. A dependent evaluation returns out_of_frame, naming the undeclared definition/import/disambiguation relation and its owner, or indeterminate where admissible evidence also cannot decide the claim and that ground is given; either result names its ground. A glossary is only a locator of exact owning clauses and context declarations, cannot define either or repair missing declaration, and creates no shared default. Its indexed concept applies only through semantic-address selection of the owning clause or explicit target import.
constraints.uncertainty: The referenced FOUNDATIONS rule for alternative result grounds is not supplied beyond this local account.

conditions: A cross-context semantic relation is declared.
constraints.statement: The owner-authorised carrier states exact source/target concept references and context identities; kind; direction and material lawful inverse; preserved/changed meaning, loss and refusal conditions; semantic owners without authority transfer; selected source/target bases, scope/provenance; lifecycle/invalidation. Owners are authorities, distinct from referenced owning clauses. FOUNDATIONS' member import rule applies between any two declared contexts: changed, narrowed or lost source meaning is not an unchanged-meaning import. No kind widens either authority. Specialisation additionally identifies exact target, preserved/narrowed meanings, excluded source instances and absence/law of inverse; its label alone establishes nothing.
constraints.uncertainty: AC-012 correspondence and the complete FOUNDATIONS import rule are referenced but not supplied.

grounding.quote:
- `resolves_to`: the exact selected concept reference, which is one member
  of `disambiguates`;

constraints.statement: Every local entry names decision URI, existing Product/requirement/accepted-design/other lawful owner, applicable overridden clause or resolved ambiguity, and exact scope; file category and overlay listing confer no authority. Each local_constitution.disambiguations additionally binds exact term/context, complete material candidate concept/clause references, resolves_to as one candidate, every needed semantic basis, and uri/authority/applies_to. The URI owns resolution; cross-context candidates require its complete import/translation/equivalence carrier. Empty local arrays expressly bind no entry of that kind for the Product; omission is not equivalent.

grounding.quote:
Profile availability, Product adoption and execution-scoped activation are
three distinct relations.

constraints.statement: reference_frame_bases is non-empty. Every locator names accepted declaration URI, every admitting existing lawful authority and exact governed Product/context/tenant/outcome/other scope. REFERENCE_FRAME principles/declaration shape and optional Executive profile neither select nor own a Product binding; adopting Product authority owns every grant. Selected-cut inclusion makes a profile available; only Product authority adopts it; only an exact authorised work instruction activates a bound frame for an actor and subject. Frame and actor identities remain separate. Actor names or broad frames grant no semantic, operation, review, acceptance or disposition authority beyond cited owners and exact activation.

conditions: The governed outcome crosses a chain of Products.

grounding.quote:
Every directed
Product-composition edge names its source and target roles, governing
authority and contracts, lifecycle, evidence boundary, refusal and
invalidation conditions.

constraints.statement: Record a Product-role map distinguishing mutable source projects, Product Definitions, candidate checkpoints, release cuts, released Products, installs, artifacts and dependent Products; development products are role bindings over exact underlying install identity. Every directed composition edge names roles, governing authority/contracts, lifecycle, evidence boundary and refusal/invalidation. Shared actors, repositories, files, implementations, outputs or tool access create neither composition nor identity.
constraints.uncertainty: SPEC_METHOD §6's full lineage definitions are outside the supplied source.

conditions: A starter frame-basis template is adopted, or a Product/domain/runtime carrier is named Frame.

grounding.quote:
It enters the collective
frame set only through an explicit frame declaration with the required
evaluation and authority relations (P1, P3).

constraints.statement: PROJECT_REFERENCE_FRAME_BASIS_TEMPLATE.md is a copyable projection, not authority. Adoption replaces every placeholder with exact identities, owners, scopes, sources, grants, results and invalidators, then admits the completed declaration under existing authority. A same-named Frame carrier stays governed by its bound WHAT/HOW, may be an evaluation subject/coordinate, and joins the collective frame set only by explicit declaration with required evaluation and authority relations.

grounding.quote:
A separate
`TENANT_REGISTRY.md` may remain as a human-readable companion or generated
projection and cannot become a second tenant-identity or location
authority (P3, P6).

constraints.statement: A separate TENANT_REGISTRY.md may be a readable companion/generated projection but cannot become a second tenant identity/location authority. Tenant surfaces declare their SPEC_METHOD §11-governed binding. Work locator choice does not transfer Goals, ticket-state or commentary authority.
constraints.uncertainty: The detailed tenant-binding and carrier-selection laws reside in unsupplied members.

conditions: A requested Product scope is discovered and composition resolved.

grounding.quote:
For a requested Product scope exactly one applicable definition is
selected; zero or several unresolved definitions fail closed, and a
symlinked definition is refused

constraints.statement: Select exactly one applicable definition; zero or several unresolved definitions fail closed, and symlinked definitions are refused. Nesting creates no inheritance, ownership, composition or override. Each composition entry names target locator, expected product.definition_id, authority defining directed kind/source-target roles/owner/scope/lifecycle/invalidation, and a non-empty exact governing contract set. Resolve both locator and expected identity. Movement needs locator update but preserves identity; replacement by another identity at the same locator fails closed. Exact immutable Product/release identities, when bound by an edge, must also be carried and verified by relation/contracts; mutable definition identity cannot substitute.

conditions: Conformance of a discovered definition set is claimed.

grounding.quote:
- every composition target resolves to another product definition whose
  `product.definition_id` equals `target_definition_id`, and every
  relation and non-empty contract set resolves; and
- no two carriers claim authority for the same Product, tenant, ticket
  state or constitutional relation.

constraints.statement: Every definition validates against its selected released schema; every required URI/fragment resolves within declared workspace/resolver boundaries; definition IDs are globally unique in the set and tenant IDs unique within each overlay. Every governed scope has an applicable resolvable frame basis and overlapping bases reconcile through cited authority. Every disambiguation carries exact term/context/complete candidates/selected member/authority/bases/scope with a congruent carrier. Every material cross-context seam uses explicit import/disambiguation/translation/equivalence. Every composition target matches expected identity, and every relation/non-empty contract set resolves. No two carriers claim the same Product, tenant, ticket-state or constitutional-relation authority.

conditions: Definition conformance is evaluated.
exceptions: JSON Schema uri and uri-reference formats assert syntax only when the declared validator implements format assertion; otherwise they are annotations.

grounding.quote:
The structural subset and
the semantic subset of these checks are distinct claims

constraints.statement: Portable Draft 2020-12 JSON Schema establishes structural shape. Conformance explicitly checks RFC 3986 URI/URI-reference syntax using an assertion-capable validator, then separately checks resolution, fragment existence, selected-release identity, cross-file uniqueness, constitutional sufficiency, semantic resolution/cross-context relation completeness and authority congruence. Structural and semantic subsets are distinct claims.

conditions: Conformance is evaluated under an exact selected basis.

grounding.quote:
Correct
downstream behaviour produced through a guessed meaning does not pass
semantic conformance (P6, P1).

constraints.statement: Cover uniquely resolved use and material collisions at minimum. Without explicit cross-context relations, Frame carriers cannot enrol by name, Owner evaluation families gain no owner authority, Product senses select only by occurrence context, and build Tenant supplies no other-tenancy default. Positive local cases declare one context/exactly one concept; positive cross-context cases provide complete authorised relations. Negative cases include zero candidates, multiple after disambiguation, selection outside candidates, context-free glossary fallback, incomplete coordinates, authority/basis mismatch, undeclared loss and invalidated relations. Correct downstream behaviour reached by guessing does not pass.

exceptions: A concrete form is method law when explicitly accepted by the method as an interoperability boundary, as referenced for the definition schema/template.

grounding.quote:
A shared-method amendment cannot create an executable tool, workflow
engine, runtime, assurance system or consumer realisation as STDO Product
scope without separate explicit human authorisation.

constraints.statement: Consumers own instantiated types/schemas, files, tools, runtime/orchestration, tests and executable conformance. A shared-method amendment cannot create executable tooling, workflow engines, runtime, assurance systems or consumer realisation as STDO Product scope without separate explicit human authorisation. An agent recording a ruling cannot widen subject, implication, authority or change class. Only released versions are publication authority; mutable authoring may construct a future cut but cannot silently govern consumers.

conditions: Derived instructions operate within their declared scope, or a released/installed derived carrier is treated as current.

grounding.quote:
A projected prohibition cannot lose its condition
or its lawful alternative, even when every source digest is correct.

constraints.statement: Preserve owning-clause applicability, obligations, permissions, exclusions, decision owners and invalidators; prohibitions retain conditions and lawful alternatives even with correct digests. Compression cannot strengthen or weaken required relations. References must resolve within actor access or required meaning must be supplied directly. Each cut/installation-derived carrier records paths/digests of every deciding source and watched index. Any such digest change makes it stale; regeneration or explicit re-acceptance is required before installation treats it current. Raw owning members of the same selected cut decide questions a stale/insufficient carrier cannot decide.
constraints.uncertainty: Full standalone-scope, staleness and matching-digest law is referenced to ACTIVATION, GLOSSARY and EVALUATION outside the supplied sections.

conditions: A Product is bootstrapped under the described method.

grounding.quote:
14. Validate the JSON shape, assert URI and URI-reference syntax,
    synchronise and verify the exact installed basis, then resolve every
    URI and perform the cross-definition identity, composition,
    constitutional-sufficiency and authority-congruence checks.

constraints.statement: The stated sequence is: (1) install manager once, resolve a version-line selector, explicitly select immutable RC; (2) install complete cut/shared store and retain deterministic manifest digest; (3) copy that cut's definition template; (4) assign stable mutable definition-line ID, source-project locator and context, distinct from immutable Product/release IDs; (5) bind constitution source, non-operative selector, exact basis/digest, all additional authorities and basis-qualified entrypoints, confirming joint axioms/ontology/epistemology/taxonomy/semantics sufficiency; (6) bind bootstrap and portable targets relative to resolved source_project, preflight every target and install/refresh only marker-bounded discovery blocks; (7) bind or explicitly empty local axiom/override/disambiguation collections; (8) bind at least one accepted collective frame basis, admitting authorities and exact scope; (9) confirm/write Goals, perform Goals→Intent→Product steps and bind entrypoints; (10) gather/derive/classify/bind live specifications without co-equal rival; (11) bind at least one tenant with root/design/implementation and any shared law; (12) bind Goals, ticket lanes, comments and optional sprints; (13) explicitly bind every known composition edge with expected target identity, relation authority and non-empty contracts; (14) perform structural/syntax checks, synchronise/verify exact install, then URI, identity, composition, sufficiency and authority checks.
constraints.uncertainty: This is a representation of a source-prescribed sequence, not its execution; earlier constitutional-sufficiency and manager-marker details are unsupplied.

exceptions: A project-local exact method copy is lawful when explicitly bound and verified; it is not the default and proximity cannot select it.
constraints.statement: Mutable method authoring in its source workspace governs a future candidate only; selected exact immutable release owns released methodology authority; installed distribution normally resides in the shared manager store and matches basis URI/manifest digest; project constitutional surfaces are at what bindings and realisation/work at how/ticketing. Create no competing local methodology root and bind no mutable/partial source as the immutable release. Resolved installed basis remains operative until explicit adoption of another cut. Once a requirement set is live, a rival monolithic requirement document should not remain co-equal; this recommendation prescribes no folder.

exceptions: The traversal record and F_D/F_P/F_H are tier-1 AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §5 terms; generic module is unrestricted.

grounding.quote:
The traversal record and the functor kinds F_D,
F_P and F_H are tier-1 calculus terms owned by AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §5, and
"module" is a generic term, as the predecessor's generic testing law uses
it; neither is restricted here.

constraints.statement: The core names no runtime, carrier or executor. Externally owned profile/realisation/rc.2 terms—graph, edge, vector, ledger, event log, worksite, HoG, Markov overlay, screen, entity cut, IACS and Prime—enter neither tier 1 nor 2 except disposition tables. Profiles may declare bindings with direction/preserved meaning/narrowed scope/invalidation. Each imports every used tier-1/2 concept and generic family under FOUNDATIONS, restating none of that member's rules; family-table premise columns cite family ID and owning table section, with owner-defined consequence standing. A profile refining another declares this in its lead; the refined owner retains rules and the refiner owns additions only. Added choices cannot masquerade as foundation consequences. Worked applications, hello worlds and data mappers are external test subjects, not precedents creating generic functionality.
constraints.uncertainty: Complete import/family-standing rules and the ODD provenance body are not supplied.

conditions: A predecessor row has no disposition.

grounding.quote:
a
row with none is unresolved, which blocks qualification of the claim it
affects.

constraints.statement: Each predecessor disposition must be one of the four RELEASE §9 values. A missing disposition remains unresolved and blocks qualification of the affected claim; it is not conserved, superseded or false by default.
constraints.uncertainty: The four RELEASE §9 values and full predecessor rows are not included here.

grounding.quote:
The corpus is applicable
without the rc.2 cut, which remains the operative builder of this
construction until this candidate is released.

constraints.statement: Tier 1/2 and project-selected tier-3 profiles are constitutional members. Clauses name requiring principles; predecessor routes are provenance, not dispositions. Each member records received-row dispositions in its last section and the frontier records every predecessor disposition/locus. The candidate describes itself as applicable without predecessor-body dependence while rc.2 remains its operative builder until release. Verbatim frames become stale when member digests mismatch; ACTIVATION §2 governs frame versus owner acquisition. Current i3 remains partial, and historical encodings cannot be treated current.
constraints.uncertainty: The frontier, i3 README and acquisition owner are not supplied.

conditions: A consumer binds an installed method basis.
exceptions: A non-default project-local copy is possible when explicitly bound and verified.

grounding.quote:
Neither the
mutable authoring head nor the moving version-line selector silently
replaces that consumer basis

constraints.statement: The manager installs each complete immutable cut once in a shared versioned store and resolves logical release URIs. Definition basis uses logical URI and manifest digest, not a machine-local path. Installed-byte authority derives from exact RC cut, definition basis URI, manifest digest and member inventory. Mutable authoring head and moving version-line selector do not silently replace consumer basis. Optional occurrence-profile adoption neither changes calculus nor selects a consumer.
constraints.uncertainty: Detailed installation and exact-cut qualification contracts are referenced elsewhere.

conditions: The reference-frame engagement law is applied or specialised.

grounding.quote:
It is engagement law only: it defines no application
profile, role mapping, product-owned frame-basis binding, domain product,
specification taxonomy, design ontology, runtime, workflow, adoption
relation or assurance implementation.

constraints.statement: Engagement law does not define application profiles, role maps, Product frame-basis bindings, domain Products, specification taxonomies, design ontology, runtime, workflow, adoption or assurance implementation. Other members/Products may import or specialise under their authority; those external relations neither enter nor amend this member. Same-spelled profiles, Products, roles or runtime carriers are not imported by proximity/name. Engagement atomicity does not collapse semantic atoms or owners.

grounding.quote:
A refinement this member states, such as the function outcomes of §5
or the coverage statuses of §8, names its owner in this table and maps
back to it. A frame or frame family that a profile or product declares in
this context is that owner's specialisation under Scope above and is not
imported here (P1, P3, P6).

constraints.statement: Every listed import runs from its named source member to reference-frame-evaluation with no loss, ownership transfer or authority conferral. Scope claims do not redefine imported evaluation, basis, activation, core results or qualification. Local refinements, including function outcomes/coverage statuses, name and map back to their imported owner. Profile/Product frame families in this context are that owner's specialisations, not imports into this member. Each concept keeps one owning section.

allowed: An owning document, section, schema field, operation or other surface may explicitly declare context for all subordinate occurrences.
Uniquely resolved prose need not repeat a qualifier on each term.
forbidden: Treating proximity, filename, heading, glossary match, repository, directory, prompt, actor or nearby definition as an accidental context declaration.

grounding.quote:
A document, section, schema field, operation or other owning surface may
declare a context for all subordinate occurrences, so uniquely resolved
prose need not repeat a qualifier on every term.

allowed: An accepted frame basis may be entirely source-linked prose.
A declaration may adopt an available profile or define a project configuration.
Several agents may activate overlapping frame subsets; one agent may activate different frames over time.
The copyable template may be used with every placeholder replaced and the result admitted by existing authority.
forbidden: Requiring a schema, axiomatic representation, prompt framework or runtime frame engine merely to use the method.
Treating a template or JSON locator as frame-set authority.

grounding.quote:
An accepted Project Reference-Frame Basis may be expressed entirely as
source-linked prose.

allowed: Work-carrier bindings may resolve to directories, repository resources, tracker collections, API endpoints or product-scoped queries.
Specification may cite multiple surfaces; a readable/generated tenant registry companion may coexist without second authority.
forbidden: A companion tenant registry becoming a second tenant-identity or location authority.

grounding.quote:
These bindings may resolve to directories,
repository resources, tracker collections, API endpoints or product-scoped
queries.

allowed: An existing project binds its current layout without moving, renaming or duplicating authority/realisation surfaces.
Default paths and folder shape may vary through URI bindings.
Multiple named definitions may share a monorepo root and bind different WHATs; one or more definitions may occur at any nested project root.
A complete requirements tree is not required on day zero.

Requirements may come from any legitimate constitutional input regardless of path, including Goals, Intent, Product, existing requirements, imported standards/policy, prior versions and migration/repricing sources.
The usual Goals→Intent→Product→requirements derivation is not the only lawful requirement source.
A project-local exact copy is lawful when explicitly bound and verified.
forbidden: Treating starter topology as universal path law or a conformance requirement.
Inferring Product composition from directory nesting.
Selecting a local method copy by proximity or binding mutable/partial method source as the immutable release.

grounding.quote:
that is the usual starting point, not the only lawful source
(P2).

allowed: A reference frame may use prose, structured data, prompt, design asset, typed carrier, runtime context or any other consumer-selected form.
Other owners may import or specialise engagement relations under their own authority.
forbidden: Requiring a class, aggregate, actor, controller, service, registry, graph or frame engine.
Treating external specialisation as an amendment to the owning engagement-law member.

grounding.quote:
A reference frame may be represented in prose, structured data,
a prompt, a design asset, a typed carrier, a runtime context or any other
form its consumer selects. No class, aggregate, actor, controller, service,
registry, graph or frame engine is required (P2; RF-016).

limitations: This is an F_P source interpretation only. It performs no semantic acceptance, operation, installation, qualification or completeness judgment.
Only the supplied sections are interpreted. Graphify nodes and edges outside them supply no normative endpoints, missing definitions or governing dependencies.

Referenced FOUNDATIONS, ACTIVATION, EVALUATION, RELEASE, SPEC_METHOD, TICKETS, profile bodies, schemas, templates, frontier and interpretation files are not available except through the supplied descriptions. Their definitions and procedures are not fabricated.

Catalogues aggregate named concepts and routes to retain material distinctions compactly. Aggregation does not assert identity across documents or turn indexed ownership into independently verified authority.

Source-described judgments, traversals, transformations and ordered workflows are represented as data in concepts and constraints. No operational records or executed populations are created; the requested adapter's judgment, traversal and transformation populations remain empty.
